title: Act 1 — Screw Around and Find Out
summary: Sameer realises the voice note was not spoken by Parth: the voice is deep and mocking, as if run through a voice modulator. He goes to Parth's home and, with his mother's permission, searches Parth's room, where a riddle leads him to a coded diary, and the decoded phrase unlocks Parth's laptop. The laptop holds files on missing people who all vanished under a full moon and a map screenshot pointing to an abandoned field, where he finds a silver sedan and a backpack of cassettes. A cassette of chanting and drums sends him running from a cyber cafe; the car is traced to a man named Vihaan, and an old home video shows Vihaan playing the same kind of drums Sameer heard on the tape.

colour_legend.red: A player question and the answer chosen in the draft (the "Ans :" lines). In the game these become autoplay questions.
colour_legend.blue: Not used in Act 1: the pasted text contains no penalty branches, so no choice below has penalty true.

beats.title: The Wrong Voice
beats.description: Sameer shivers as the voice note plays: something is off about the voice, as if it has gone through a voice modulator. It is not Parth's. It is deep and mocking, as though making fun of his distress, and he feels it reverberating in his skull and grating in his ears. He decides to go to Parth's room.
beats.media_notes: Voice-only character: the audio must sound pitch-shifted and modulated, deep and mocking. The poem from the Act 0 voice note is the audio being reacted to and must stay word for word. Not a playable room yet.

beats.title: Meeting Parth's Mom
beats.description: Sameer goes to Parth's home. Parth's mother look as if she has not slept since the day her son went missing, but she still smiled at him, with great effort. After some small talk, with a lump in his throat, Sameer says: "I would like to go to Parth's room, aunty." His mother looks up the stairs with unshed tears, looks back at Sameer, then allows it. She croaks out: "Please don't disturb anything in his room, Parth may have a hard time finding stuff once he comes back." Sameer runs up the stairs.
beats.media_notes: Heavy, quiet mood; forced smiles. The mother's request not to disturb anything is also stored as the fact room_left_untouched.

beats.title: The Locked Laptop
beats.description: Sameer finds himself in Parth's room. He sits on the unmade bed and looks around for a clue. His gaze falls on the open laptop, in sleep mode, as if Parth had been working on it, and he starts his investigation there. It is password protected. He says: "Looks like I need to guess the password." The guess is wrong, and the screen shows a hint: "Look where my loudest secrets are kept, away from prying eyes, leather bound and stained with ink."
beats.media_notes: Autoplay questions guess_password and laptop_riddle fire inside this beat. The hint text is the riddle exactly as written.

beats.title: The Diary
beats.description: Sameer reaches up to the bookshelf and finds a leather diary with a gold engraving of the moon and stars. The first page carries a quote. Flipping through, he finds a page of dots and dashes, and the next page is a decoder with each pattern matching a letter. He realises he has to sit and decode it by hand, and wonders why Parth could not write normally. The decoded letters read "OC1808 in laptop". Sameer finds this a very strange thing to encode but shelves it for later. The rest of the diary is useless because Parth's handwriting is practically unreadable.
beats.media_notes: Autoplay question decode_diary fires here. The quote on the first page is shown as "..." in the source and still needs to be written. The dot-and-dash page and the decoder page need to be designed as zoom-in exhibit images.

beats.title: Inside the Laptop
beats.description: Sameer types the decoded phrase into the laptop and says, in the worst hacker voice in existence, "Heh, I'm in." In the folders he finds reports and posters of missing people, all of whom disappeared under the full moon. One of the men has a huge hooked nose and a horribly thick nose ring. He mails the contents of the folder to himself. He also finds a screenshot of a map area with coordinates, plus a few corrupted files he is too impatient to look at. He enters the coordinates into Boogle maps and they lead to an abandoned field that looks like the kind of place one would get kidnapped at.
beats.media_notes: The map app is named "Boogle maps" in the source and is kept as written. Show the poster of the hooked-nose man in close-up. The corrupted files are visible but not openable.

beats.title: The Abandoned Field
beats.description: Sameer walks to the abandoned field, which is not far from Parth's home. He checks out a dusty but luxurious silver sedan with the number plate KA01OC1808. On the seat is a black backpack; he opens it and finds a few cassettes. He looks around and finds no one: the place is completely deserted, like an old cowboy movie minus the tumbleweed. In a very unsuspicious way he picks up the bag and leaves as quickly as possible.
beats.media_notes: Deserted, dusty, western-film feel. Sameer takes the backpack with him.

beats.title: The Cassette
beats.description: Sameer remembers an old cyber cafe near Ramu's dosa corner that runs Windows XP and has cassette players lying around. After some time finding a working player, he inserts one of the cassettes. The mixtape begins with a faint crackling sound, then ritualistic chanting, weird drum sounds and bizarre words he cannot place in any language. There is a scream and then nothing. Scared for his life, Sameer grabs the bag and runs, with the shopkeeper screaming at him to pay for the device.
beats.media_notes: Audio is the key asset: crackle, chanting, drums, unintelligible words, a scream, then silence. The drum sound must be distinct enough to be recognised again in the home video.

beats.title: Vihaan
beats.description: Holy hell, he should never have opened that abandoned car. Sameer feels the world spin, then come to an abrupt stop. He pulls out his phone and looks up information about the car. After some time he retrieves the owner's details: the car belongs to a person named Vihaan. He hopes Vihaan is somehow connected to his missing friend and not a useless side quest.
beats.media_notes: Short phone-screen beat; the location is not stated in the source.

beats.title: The Home Videos
beats.description: Sameer goes back to Parth's home and asks Parth's mother about anyone named Vihaan. She is a bit confused: he was a childhood friend, and there are a few home videos. The grainy video shows a younger Parth and Vihaan, with Vihaan playing the drums. Sameer recognises the drum sound he has just heard. He looks through every video of Parth and Vihaan but finds nothing else, and with a resigned look says farewell to Parth's mother and leaves.
beats.media_notes: Parth and Vihaan appear only as children in grainy home-video footage. Autoplay question where_heard_drums fires after the drum moment. Act ends when Sameer leaves.

characters.name: Sameer
characters.persona: DRAFT — the player's point of view. Loyal, anxious, talks fast when stressed. He is the one who searches, asks, and refuses to let it go; under pressure he jokes (the worst hacker voice in existence) and keeps going.
goals: Hold everything together for Parth's mother
characters.notes: Never interrogated — players play as him. Same id as in Act 0.

characters.name: Parth
characters.notes: Still missing. In Act 1 he appears only as a child in the grainy home video with Vihaan, and through his room, diary and laptop. His handwriting is practically unreadable.

characters.name: Parth's mother
characters.persona: DRAFT — worn out and holding herself together with effort. She still smiles for Sameer, calls him beta, and speaks plainly even when her voice breaks. She is protective of Parth's room and everything in it.
goals: Keep Parth's room exactly as he left it

facts.text: She asks Sameer not to disturb anything in Parth's room, because Parth may have a hard time finding his things once he comes back.
Vihaan was a childhood friend, and there are a few home videos of him and Parth.

characters.notes: Same id as in Act 0. Set interrogable to false if her Act 1 exchanges stay scripted and cinematic. Deflections, snubs and the last voice example are writer-drafted, not taken from the source. In the source the Vihaan fact reads that he was a childhood friend "of Sameer", but the home videos show Parth and Vihaan, so it is probably a typo for Parth; the fact text is worded neutrally until the writers confirm.

contradictions.they_claim: The voice note arrives as a message from Parth.
contradictions.the_truth: The voice is not Parth's; it is deep, mocking and apparently run through a voice modulator. Who is speaking is not yet decided.

truth.spoiler_notes: Culprit, method and motive are unknown until the remaining acts are written. Threads the source plants but does not resolve: the missing people who all vanished under a full moon, the man with the hooked nose and nose ring, the ritual cassette with drums, the car registered to Vihaan and Vihaan's drumming. Do not read any of them as an accusation yet.

act_flow.starts_when: The player has listened to the voice note (end of Act 0) and the modulated voice reaction plays.
act_flow.ends_when: Sameer finds nothing more in the home videos, says farewell to Parth's mother and leaves.
act_flow.carries_over: The clues voice_not_parth, laptop_hint, moon_diary, coded_page, missing_persons_files, hooked_nose_man, map_coordinates, sedan_plate, backpack_cassettes, mixtape_recording, car_owner_vihaan and home_video_drums; the character Vihaan and the drum link; the missing-people files Sameer mailed to himself; the black backpack of cassettes Sameer took; and Sameer's unpaid debt at the cyber cafe. Sameer remains the player's point of view.

notes: Open decisions for writers: (1) is_cinematic is null because the source reads as a linear story with questions, yet it contains room, hotspot and clue structure; decide whether Act 1 is playable exploration or authored playback. (2) The diary's first-page quote is "..." in the source and needs to be written. (3) The dot-and-dash patterns and decoder table, and the exact laptop password, are not in the source. (4) The source says Vihaan was a childhood friend "of Sameer", but the home videos show Parth and Vihaan; likely a typo for Parth, so the fact is worded neutrally. (5) The map app is named "Boogle maps" in the source and is kept as written. (6) Rooms unlock in order: parth_home first, then abandoned_field after map_coordinates, then cyber_cafe after backpack_cassettes. (7) The source has no penalty branches in Act 1, so every choice has penalty false, and distractor choices are left null placeholders as in Act 0. (8) Hotspot positions are null; the build team will place them. (9) Ids sameer, parth, parth_mother and parth_home are reused from Act 0 on purpose; all other ids are new. (10) The Act 0 voicemail clue should now note that the voice is not Parth's.
